hints: Apply the tangent addition formula and replace $\cot x$ by $1/\tan x$.
With $t=\tan x$ and $\tan45^\circ=1$, clear denominators to obtain a quadratic equation in $t$.
Solve the quadratic for both tangent values, then use tangent's $180^\circ$ period to find every $x$ satisfying $0^\circ<x<180^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Apply the compound angle identity $\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A\tan B}$ to the left-hand side with $A = x$ and $B = 45^\circ$:
Using $\tan 45^\circ = 1$:
$$\tan(x + 45^\circ) = \dfrac{\tan x + 1}{1 - \tan x}$$

Express $\cot x$ in terms of $\tan x$ as $\cot x = \dfrac{1}{\tan x}$:
$$\dfrac{\tan x + 1}{1 - \tan x} = \dfrac{2}{\tan x}$$

Multiply both sides by $\tan x(1 - \tan x)$ to clear denominators:
$$\tan x(\tan x + 1) = 2(1 - \tan x)$$
$$\tan^2 x + \tan x = 2 - 2\tan x$$

Rearrange all terms to the left-hand side to obtain a quadratic equation in $\tan x$:
$$\tan^2 x + 3\tan x - 2 = 0$$

Solve the quadratic equation using the quadratic formula with $a = 1, b = 3, c = -2$:
$$\tan x = \dfrac{-3 \pm \sqrt{3^2 - 4(1)(-2)}}{2(1)} = \dfrac{-3 \pm \sqrt{9 + 8}}{2} = \dfrac{-3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{2}$$

Evaluate the first root where $\tan x > 0$:
$$\tan x = \dfrac{-3 + \sqrt{17}}{2} \approx \dfrac{-3 + 4.12311}{2} = \dfrac{1.12311}{2} \approx 0.56155$$
$$x = \arctan(0.56155) \approx 29.32^\circ \implies x \approx 29.3^\circ$$

Evaluate the second root where $\tan x < 0$ in the range $0^\circ < x < 180^\circ$:
$$\tan x = \dfrac{-3 - \sqrt{17}}{2} \approx \dfrac{-3 - 4.12311}{2} = \dfrac{-7.12311}{2} \approx -3.56155$$
$$x = 180^\circ + \arctan(-3.56155) \approx 180^\circ - 74.32^\circ = 105.68^\circ \implies x \approx 105.7^\circ$$

State all solutions in the interval $0^\circ < x < 180^\circ$ correct to 1 decimal place:
$$x = 29.3^\circ, \quad 105.7^\circ$$
